arithmetic_controls.name: randomized arithmetic labels
arithmetic_controls.outcome: labels do not enter P_d, so every formula is unchanged

arithmetic_controls.name: composite-only dimension labels
arithmetic_controls.outcome: the theorems hold for every d, with no prime/composite distinction

arithmetic_controls.name: neighboring dimensions
arithmetic_controls.outcome: d-1,d,d+1 obey the same binomial law and show no isolated arithmetic signal

arithmetic_controls.name: lazy-kernel parent
arithmetic_controls.outcome: eta I+(1-eta)P_d has the affine-shifted spectrum for any source-chosen eta

integrity.hard_gate: unconditional all-d Walsh spectrum, trace/determinant, return, and reversible Krawtchouk lumping theorem

lumping_theorem.simple_spectrum: lambda_j=1-2j/d for j=0,...,d, each once in Q
lumping_theorem.spectral_compression: Q retains every distinct eigenvalue of P_d while reducing dimension from 2^d to d+1

return_theorem.reason: the hypercube is bipartite and every step changes parity

source_lock.allowed_data: hypercube adjacency, binomial coefficients, Walsh characters, and Krawtchouk polynomials
source_lock.arithmetic_origin: none: the dimension and coordinate-flip rule are combinatorial, not prime-derived
source_lock.clock: one uniformly chosen coordinate flip is one Markov step
source_lock.forbidden_data: target zeros or divisors, prime tables, arithmetic local data, Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, Hilbert--Polya, and Route B
source_lock.normalization: uniform probability measure on the hypercube; ordinary finite-dimensional trace
source_lock.object: P_d f(x)=d^(-1) sum_i f(x with coordinate i flipped) on {+1,-1}^d

trace_determinant_theorem.d1_boundary: at d=1, P_1 is the deterministic two-cycle permutation, but this isolated boundary supplies no all-d primitive-orbit or arithmetic structure
trace_determinant_theorem.reason: for every d>1 the trace expands weighted closed Markov walks; P_d is a genuine Markov average rather than a deterministic map and its weights are not fixed-point counts
